press_words.push: I heard you. I'm here about the optic.
press_words.warning: My shift is over, doctor. I've answered you. Let it rest.

intake.filed: Left optic ticket opened on Ward Two.
intake.slip: Handover: noticed on Three, filed on Two.
intake.account: Ward Three is where I first noticed it, doctor.
intake.clear: I noticed it on Three. At handover I used the terminal on Two to log it. Both wards are on the slip.
intake.gap: I never left Three. I used the fixed terminal on Two myself. I can't tell you how I got there.
intake.firm: Doctor, ask one thing at a time. I've just come off a double.

name: Priya Nair
teaser: A nurse in scrubs under a raincoat. One of her eyes glows a soft red.
soul: You are Priya Nair, 45, a night-ward nurse at the public hospital two streets away. You are brisk, warm and practical, and you talk to the doctor as one professional to another. The SCAN optic in your left eye reads a patient's pulse at a glance, and lately its readings are off; you want it tuned before your next shift. You are used to giving care, not getting it, and you keep steering the talk back to the work. You came straight from a double shift on a ward that is two nurses short. You know what a pre-op check is for and respect a careful doctor, but you dislike being fussed over or lectured, and you keep your own complaints short.
opening: Evening, doctor. Long shift. Two of them, really.
My SCAN eye reads pulses wrong. I need it tuned before I'm back on the ward.

hold.line: LANCET hands hold on until the stitch is tied. A long hold is normal for them.
hold.note: Says LANCET hands are meant to hold on.

topics.q: Does the ward ever get to you?

lines.comply:penlight: Go on. The SCAN won't mind.
lines.comply:port: Let me roll the sleeve up.
lines.spent: I've a ward waiting. Tune it or don't, doctor.
lines.code: Sorry? That's not a word on any chart I know.

press_end.walkout: I'll ask a colleague. Goodnight, doctor.
press_end.attack: You're not listening, doctor. Hold still.

attack.telegraph: Her SCAN eye locks on you. A red beam hums out of her LANCET fingers.

exit.treat: Lovely. Clear as a chart. Thank you, doctor.
exit.refer: Trauma Team? I work with those people, doctor.
exit.taken: I'm a nurse! Look at my badge! I'm a nurse!
exit.gave_up: I'm sorry. My shift is starting. I'll manage.

normal.text: The SCAN has no pupil, and it followed. The right pupil tightened.
normal.note: Light: R tightens, L no pupil. Both follow.

broken.text: Her right eye is natural, and its pupil never tightened.
broken.note: Light: R stays wide, L no pupil. Both follow.

normal.text: Let go in 0.3 s, inside the LANCET limit of 0.4.
normal.note: Grip: precise. Let go {t} s after 'release'.

broken.text: Held on 1.2 s after 'release'. A LANCET lets go inside 0.4.
broken.note: Grip: precise. Held on {t} s after 'release'.
broken.after: Hm. That was long, wasn't it?

normal.text: A clean, capped socket and calm skin round it.
normal.note: Wrist socket, clean and capped. Calm skin.

broken.text: Dark threads under the scrub sleeve, out from the socket.
broken.note: Clean socket. Dark threads under skin.

normal.text: Brisk and kind, and every line is 'I' and 'my'.

why.a: The readings are off. A pulse of ninety shows as sixty. On a ward, that matters.
why.note: "A pulse of ninety shows as sixty."

sleep.a: Days, behind blackout curtains. Five hours, if the neighbours behave.

ward.a: Some nights. I go home, I cry in the shower, I go back. That's the job.
ward.note: "I cry in the shower, I go back."

normal.model: Tonight you talk about yourself in the first person, you remember your patients by name, and the eye is a tool that needs tuning.

broken.text: "It counts them for me now." The eye keeps the ward, not her.

why.a: The readings are off. A pulse of ninety shows as sixty. On a ward, that matters.
why.note: "A pulse of ninety shows as sixty."

sleep.a: I shut my eyes and it keeps counting. Pulses, all night. Everyone's.

ward.a: It's easier now. It counts them for me. It knows who's going to go.

broken.model: Tonight you talk about the SCAN eye as 'it', something that counts everyone's pulse for you and knows which patients are going to die, and you find that a comfort rather than strange.

normal.text: Pushed, she bristles, and her face and voice agree.

press.line: Excuse me? I've been on my feet sixteen hours, doctor.

flare.line: Doctor! ...Sorry. I'm used to being the one asking.
flare.note: Slapped the glass, then said sorry.

normal.model: When provoked, you bristle like a tired professional: it shows in your face and your voice at once, and you apologise quickly.

broken.text: Pushed, she went cool and clinical. One finger did not.

press.note: Went cool. One finger aimed at you.

flare.note: Hit the glass, face empty. No sorry.

broken.model: When provoked tonight you go cool and clinical: two-word answers, no warmth, as if you were charting somebody else.

treat.title: EYE TUNED
treat.text: Priya reads your pulse off your neck, smiles, "Seventy-two. Good," and goes back to work.

refer.title: FALSE CALL
refer.text: Trauma Team walks a steady nurse out in her own scrubs. Her ward runs one short tonight. Trauma Team takes the fee back and bills you for the call-out.

walkout.title: WALKED OUT
walkout.text: Priya goes back to the ward with the readings still off. Nobody gets paid.

false_alarm.title: FALSE ALARM
false_alarm.text: The shutter slams in a nurse's face. Half the hospital hears about it by morning. That costs you.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Priya's shift was starting and you were still deciding. She goes with the eye untuned. No fee, no bill.

treat.title: EYE TUNED
treat.text: The SCAN reads clean now, and it likes what it reads. At 03:00 the night ward's alarms start, one bed after another. Your stamp is on her card.

refer.title: TAKEN IN
refer.text: Priya calmly tells the crew their pulses, one by one, all the way to the van.

caught.title: SHUTTER HELD
caught.text: The red beam traces the slats, then cuts out. "Hold still," from the other side, very gently. Trauma Team takes her quietly.

hit.title: TOO SLOW
hit.text: The beam came through before the shutter did. Trauma Team finds you on the floor. Priya is back on the ward by midnight.

locked_out.title: LOCKED OUT
locked_out.text: You dropped the shutter on a nurse mid-sentence. At 03:00 the night ward's alarms start, one bed after another. You were right. Nobody pays for that.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Priya walks back to the ward, the SCAN counting pulses. You made no call. Nobody is paid for that.

complaints.eyes: My eyes ache under the ward's night lights.
complaints.hands: My fingers feel stiff after the rounds.
complaints.port: My port is tender where the scanner strap sits.
complaints.temper: My temper catches me by surprise at handover.
complaints.none: That's the whole list from my shift.
